sections.title: Landmarks and Where They Are
sections.content: Directions are given from landmarks, so first you need the landmarks. Then you need the phrases that place one thing against another. You already have 'al lado de' and 'cerca de'; add 'enfrente de' for opposite, and note that all three end in 'de' and so contract before 'el': enfrente del museo.

items.spanish: Estoy cerca de un banco y de una farmacia.
items.english: I'm near a bank and a chemist's.

items.spanish: La cafetería está enfrente del museo.
items.english: The café is opposite the museum.
Is there a park on the left?

items.spanish: Por fin conozco mejor la ciudad.
items.english: At last I know the city better.

sections.content: 'A la derecha' and 'a la izquierda' keep 'la' even when the thing you are placing is masculine — the 'la' belongs to an invisible 'mano', the hand. Learn the pair whole and it will never trip you up.
